bib.title: Recurrent Continuous Translation Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2013 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 1700-1709

question: Can a translation model built only on continuous representations, with a recurrent target language model conditioned on a convolutional source sentence model and no alignments or phrase units, model and rescore translations well?
hypothesis: Continuous representations and the transformations between them can make up for the lack of explicit alignments and avoid phrase-pair sparsity.
contributions: Recurrent Continuous Translation Models (RCTM I and II): target recurrent language model conditioned on a convolutional sentence model of the source
Perplexity >43% lower than alignment-based models, sensitivity to word order, syntax and meaning, and n-best rescoring matching cdec

method.summary: A recurrent language model generates the French sentence word by word; the English source is encoded by a convolutional sentence model (RCTM I, one vector added to every hidden layer) or by a truncated 4-gram convolutional model inverted to target length (RCTM II, one vector per target position, with Poisson length model). Trained jointly end to end with Adagrad and BPTT on 145k sentence pairs.
method.task: English-to-French statistical machine translation (conditional language modelling, n-best rescoring)

datasets.name: WMT 2013 news commentary En-Fr
datasets.size: 144953 sentence pairs (<80 words); about 4.1M English words and 4.5M French words
datasets.source: Eighth Workshop on Machine Translation (WMT) 2013 training data
datasets.preprocessing: words occurring twice or less replaced by <unknown>; vocabularies 25403 English and 34831 French

datasets.name: WMT-NT 2009/2010/2011/2012
datasets.preprocessing: unknown words replaced by <unknown> for perplexity

models.name: RCTM I
models.architecture: recurrent LM conditioned on CSM sentence vector added to each hidden layer

models.name: RCTM II
models.architecture: recurrent LM conditioned on per-position vectors from convolutional 4-gram model (CGM, r=7) and its inverse (icgm, s=9); Poisson target length model

models.name: cdec
models.architecture: 12-feature translation system (5 translation models, 2 LM features, word penalty)

training.objective: average of summed cross-entropy of predicted French words given English input, plus l2 regularisation

inference.decoding: for generation: sample with replacement 2000 sentences word by word, restricting each step to the top 5 words, fixed target length m = gold length; rank by model probability

parameters.rescoring: cdec 1000-best lists; RCTM log probability linearly interpolated with word penalty, weight tuned on validation data
parameters.length_model: P(m|e)=Poisson(lambda k), lambda value not given

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: perplexity of the model on reference translations

metrics.name: Bleu
metrics.definition: Bleu of 1000-best rescored output (variant not stated)

eval.protocol: single run per model; no seeds or significance tests stated

limits: Small experiment (145k pairs, q=256); authors only argue the models should scale like RLMs
Bleu differences between RCTMs and cdec are small ('little variance'); no significance tests
Used only for rescoring cdec n-best lists; no standalone decoder Bleu reported, generation shown only by sampling at gold length
RCTM I conditions every target word on one source vector; authors note target words depend on parts of source unevenly
Target length for RCTM I implicit with bias to short sentences; RCTM II uses a Poisson length model
Hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, l2 weight, Poisson lambda) not stated
No alignment or attention mechanism; superseded by sequence-to-sequence and attention models

terms.definition: Recurrent Continuous Translation Model: a target recurrent language model conditioned on a continuous representation of the source sentence
Convolutional Sentence Model: builds a sentence vector from word vectors by successive one-dimensional convolutions
